verdict.rationale: Fivetran's official MCP server is read-only by default. A `FIVETRAN_SCOPE` setting (read, read/write, read/write/delete) and a `DISALLOWED_ACTIONS` denylist that can block credential endpoints let you limit what an agent can do. Role-based access control is also listed as a platform feature. However, this scoping is enforced in the MCP server's configuration, not in the API credentials themselves, and no evidence shows issuing scoped or least-privilege API keys tied to RBAC roles. Missing for 10: documented creation of API keys with limited, role-bound permissions; per-credential resource or permission scoping on the REST API; credential lifecycle controls (expiry, rotation) for agent keys; independent or hands-on corroboration.
